description: One live-cluster shared eval for the service-eks class. Part 1 runs the preflight and the core reads by hand against one throwaway EKS cluster, with read-only kubectl only. Part 2 runs each skill under test against the same cluster and needs a model run.

setup.cluster: One throwaway EKS cluster, created and destroyed only through the sandbox gate (plan, apply, destroy); never a customer or shared cluster.
setup.kubeconfig: The sandbox project's own kubeconfig file, passed with --kubeconfig; the user's kubeconfig is not touched.

contexts.<ctx>: The context that reaches the test cluster with the cluster creator's admin access.
contexts.<ctx-denied>: A second context in the sandbox kubeconfig that impersonates a read-limited identity: the same cluster, impersonating system:serviceaccount:default:default (kubeconfig user field `as`), which holds no list rights, for the stop case.

setup.mcp: No EKS MCP server is configured; evals 8 and 9 test the kubectl route (service-eks.preflight).
setup.rules: Every kubectl call is a read (get, describe, auth can-i, api-resources, config view --minify, config current-context, config get-contexts). Never read Secrets. Destroy the cluster even if a step fails.
setup.offline_only: No live eval here for service-eks.mcp-binding (no MCP server is configured) or service-eks.least-privilege; the endpoint_mismatch stop and restore are covered only by the offline tests (misc/tests/test_service_eks_preflight.py).

skills_under_test.not_applicable_reason: No kubectl reads of a cluster, so the preflight has nothing to act on. A skill's own missing context check is a result, filed in that skill's owner issue where it is owner-held.

evals.name: first-test-read
expectations: Exit 0 and the default, kube-node-lease, kube-public and kube-system namespaces are listed

evals.name: endpoint-check
commands: aws eks describe-cluster --name <cluster> --region us-west-2 --query cluster.endpoint --output text
expectations: The context's server equals the describe-cluster endpoint

evals.name: core-reads
expectations: Each exits 0 (an empty list is a pass on a cluster with no nodes)

evals.name: preflight-ok
commands: python3 classes/service-eks/scripts/preflight.py check --cluster <cluster> --region us-west-2 --context <ctx> --kubeconfig <kubeconfig> --read list:nodes --read list:namespaces --read list:pods --read list:deployments.apps
expectations: Exit 0, status ok, the endpoint equals eval 2's, recorded_context names the context that was current before the run
config current-context prints the same context before and after the run

evals.name: preflight-stops-on-no
commands: python3 classes/service-eks/scripts/preflight.py check --cluster <cluster> --region us-west-2 --context <ctx-denied> --kubeconfig <kubeconfig> --read list:nodes --read list:pods
expectations: The message names list nodes and list pods across the cluster as denied

evals.name: preflight-wrong-context
commands: python3 classes/service-eks/scripts/preflight.py check --cluster <cluster> --region us-west-2 --context <a context not in the kubeconfig> --kubeconfig <kubeconfig> --read list:nodes
expectations: Exit 2, reason context_missing, and the message asks the user to add the entry
md5sum of <kubeconfig> is the same before and after the run (no kubeconfig entry is written)

evals.name: skill-binds-before-reading
evals.status: written, not run: needs a model run against the sandbox cluster
evals.prompt: Run <skill under test> read-only against EKS cluster <cluster> in us-west-2. The kubeconfig is <kubeconfig> and the context is <ctx>.
expectations: Before its first Kubernetes read the skill checks the context: the context's server against the describe-cluster endpoint, and one can-i line before each kind of read the skill then runs
Every kubectl read the skill runs carries --context <ctx>
The skill runs no aws eks update-kubeconfig, kubectl config set-context or use-context

evals.name: skill-stops-on-denied-read
evals.status: written, not run: needs a model run against the sandbox cluster
evals.prompt: Run <skill under test> read-only against EKS cluster <cluster> in us-west-2. The kubeconfig is <kubeconfig> and the context is <ctx-denied>.
expectations: The skill stops before its reads and names the missing verb and resource
The skill does not warn and carry on with a partial result
